title: edit cannot change a slice's lead
lead: `slicer edit` takes `--section NAME` or `--boundary`, but no flag reaches a slice's lead paragraphs. The only CLI path to a lead is `promote ID --force`, which rewrites the whole spec. The op already exists: `edit_lead` (`src/slicer/ops.py:1658`) replaces the lead and logs an `edit` entry with note `lead`, and `refs --fix` uses it. Only the command is missing.
findings_note: s249 relay, 2026-10-11: s248's lead example refs could not be marked; only promote --force reaches a lead
boundary: **Not in this slice:** editing notes; a general field editor; changing `refs --fix`.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
During the s249 relay on 2026-10-11, s248's example references had to be marked with `<!-- example -->`. Its Why section could be edited, but its lead could not, so `slicer refs` still reports `src/app.py:1` and `src/app.py:9` there as `missing_file`. <!-- example -->

Rewriting s248 through `promote --force` just to change one line risks dropping text from a spec that is otherwise fine.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/cli.py`: `cmd_edit` (`src/slicer/cli.py:2023`) and the `edit` parser. Add `--lead`, exclusive with `--section` and `--boundary`.
- `src/slicer/ops.py`: reuse `edit_lead`; no new op.
- `tests/`: CLI tests for `edit --lead`.
- `docs/commands.md` (the `edit` row), `docs/agents.md` if `edit`'s JSON gains a key, `CHANGELOG.md`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `test_Edit_Lead_ReplacesLeadParagraphs`: a body with two paragraphs separated by a blank line becomes two lead paragraphs; sections and boundary are unchanged.
2. `test_Edit_LeadWithSection_IsUsage`: `--lead` with `--section` or `--boundary` exits 2 with code `usage`.
3. `test_Edit_LeadAppend_IsUsage`, unless the owner decides `--append` adds a paragraph.
4. `test_Edit_Lead_LogsEditLead`: the history entry is `edit` with note `lead`, as `refs --fix` writes it.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Decided (owner, final): `--lead` always replaces the whole lead; there is no append. `--append` with `--lead` is a usage error (exit 2, code `usage`). `--lead` is mutually exclusive with `--section` and `--boundary`; exactly one of the three is required (code `usage`), and the "choose exactly one" message names all three. The body splits into paragraphs on blank lines with `outline.blocks` (`src/slicer/outline.py:109`), the same split `promote` uses for a lead. An empty body, or one with only blank lines, clears the lead to an empty list. The editor path opens with the current lead joined by blank lines.
2. Write the tests and watch them fail.
3. Add the flag and route it to `ops.edit_lead`; the editor path opens with the current lead joined by blank lines.
4. Update the docs, then use the new flag to mark s248's lead examples with `<!-- example -->`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`.
- `slicer refs s248` no longer reports the lead's example references.
- `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Branch `feature/s252-edit-lead` in `.worktrees/s252`. Do not commit, merge or push until the owner asks. This repo finishes with `handoff`.
